summary: Real-case protein+ligand regression of galactose oxidase (GOase) variant activity toward specific alcohol substrates.
what_it_measures: Standardized specific activity (`specific_activity_standardized`) for engineered GOase variants paired with a substrate (SMILES); i.e. variant × substrate catalytic activity.
assay_method: Experimental activity of engineered galactose oxidase variants on benzylic/secondary-alcohol substrates, from a machine-learning-guided directed-evolution campaign.
provenance: From the galactose oxidase engineering campaign of Cleveland et al. (2021): variants of one enzyme assayed against several alcohol substrates. The substrate SMILES and its concentration enter the model as features; random split, stratified on the target.
when_to_use: A realistic enzyme+substrate engineering scenario with a genuine ligand axis; tests joint reasoning over variant sequence and substrate structure.
caveats: One enzyme measured under several conditions, so rows of the same enzyme fall on both sides of the split and a tree model can match a test row to training rows of that enzyme; this favours XGBoost here. Substrates are described by the 200 normalized RDKit 2D descriptors of descriptastorus (RDKit2DNormalized).

citations.authors: e.g. Galactose oxidase machine-learning engineering studies
citations.title: A Machine Learning-Guided Approach to Navigate the Substrate Activity Scope of Galactose Oxidase
